answer: Identity proofs are then layered like velvet over that stake, so duplicating one agent costs a full bond plus wasted compute. Each agent must stake a bond locked to a unique hardware root and a slow proof-of-work challenge nicknamed the canyon, since grinding it requires real electricity. New participants start on a probationary island with capped influence until peers attest them across several epochs, making mass fakery economically irrational. From Agent0050's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
